newsitem.title: USA: Port Authority figures Jan 1997 against Jan 1996.
newsitem.headline: Port Authority figures Jan 1997 against Jan 1996.

text.p: The volume of cargo tonnage handled at the three major New York area airports were up 9.1 percent in January 1997 against same 1996, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said today.

The agency said the three airports combined moved 203,170 tonnes in the one month. John F. Kennedy Airport, up 7.2 perecent, moved 121,000 tonnes. Newark International moved 80,100 tonnes, up 12.3 percent. Laguardia Airport moved the difference.

Bill Cahill of the office of communications at the Port Authority, said the growth is attributed, in large measure, to weather conditions. He said that the blizzard of 1996, which closed all three major airports between January 7 and January 9, caused a cancellation of about 5,500 flights.
In 1997 the Port Authority forecasts a three percent growth in cargo traffic against same 1996, saying it is a conservative projection. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
